To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the C-terminus of p43 is sufficient to stimulate the ct-DNA Polymerase activity; (2) the C- terminus of p43 binds to ct-DNAPolymerase; (3) the DNA binding domain is spatially separate from DNA polymerase accessory domain; (4) DNA binding domain is glycosylated; and (5) loss of glycosylated p43 leads to repression of ct-DNAPol activity.

the C-terminal domain (p22) of p43, a pea chloroplast DNA replication accessory protein, stimulates the pea chloroplast DNA (ct) DNA polymerase activity and that the DNA binding domain (p43N) of p43 is spatially separate from its domain responsible for stimulating DNA polymerase activity.
the DNA binding domain and the DNA polymerase stimulatory domain are spatially separate in p43, and glycosylation of the DNA binding domain helps in efficient DNA polymerase activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of a DNA polymerase accessory protein from pea chloroplasts.
the characterization of p43, a chloroplast DNA replication factor, in order to understand its role and function in the chloroplast DNA replication machinery.
the elucidation of the molecular mechanism of the chloroplast DNA replication.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the carboxy terminal domain of p43 is responsible for the stimulation of ct-DNA Polymerase activity.
glycosylation of the DNA binding domain represses the DNA binding activity and hence the DNA polymerase stimulating activity of p43.
p43 is a glycosylated DNA binding accessory protein of pea ct-DNA Polymerase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the C-terminal domain (p22) of p43 is sufficient for the DNA polymerization accessory activity.
the C-terminus of p43 is a domain of high affinity for ct-DNA polymerases.
the accessory protein p43 is a multi-domain protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
p22 is the first accessory factor for DNA polymerase to be studied and it is also the first glycoprotein accessory factor to be identified.
the accessory protein of ct-DNA Polymerase has evolved a unique mechanism to regulate DNA polymerase activity.
glycosylation of a protein can play a regulatory role by altering the conformation of the protein and thus the protein-protein interaction.
